1  JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Vijaya Kumar who met with road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief are that : On 17.01.2021 at about 00.50 a.m., the deceased Vijaya Kumar and others were returning to Bengaluru in Canter lorry bearing No.KA-02-C-8008 and when they reached near Metatukri of Hariyuru Taluk, the said Center lorry got punctured.
Since it was midnight no mechanic was available, they decided to stop the vehicle by the side of road.
They got down from the vehicle and some of them slept in front of the vehicle and some of them were sitting,

at that time the driver of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AC-2285 by coming from Davanagere to Bengaluru side on NH-4 road in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, lost control over the vehicle, dashed against the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008, result of which the vehicle which was stationed moved ahead and ran over the persons, who were slept in front of the vehicle and the deceased Vijaya Kumar was succumbed to fatal injuries.
So far, the petitioner has spent about Rs.1,50,000/- towards funeral obsequious ceremonies.
3. Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy.
The deceased was working as stunt master in Cinema Industry, thereby earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden demise of deceased, the petitioner has sustained mental and physical hardship.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-AC-2285 and the respondent no.2 being the RC owner of the Canter vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

4. The respondent No.1- the RC owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-AC-2285 has filed written statement and contended that the canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 was parked on the road without putting any indicators and as such the alleged accident was on account of the negligent act on the part of the driver of canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 .
It is further contended that there is no rash and negligent on the part of the 1st respondent.
The police have colluded with the petitioner and filed false case against him.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 - Sri.Manjunath Swamy the R.C. the owner of Canter vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 remained absent, hence he was placed ex-parte.

6. On the basis of the rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Vijaya Kumar ?

2. Whether the petitioner proves that Vijay Kumar was died on account of road traffic accident on 17.01.2021 at about 0.50 a.m., NH-road, near Metikurke village of Hiriyuru Taluk, Chitradurga District on due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AC-2285?

Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67624714/
2 3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.

What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked in all 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed her side.

The respondent no.1 examined himself as RW.1.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue no 3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following; REASONS 10.Issue No.1: The petitioner has stated that she is the only legal representatives of the deceased.

In support of the same the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card of the petitioner and deceased and Ration card of the family of petitioner at Ex.P7 and 8 which reveals that petitioner is the mother of deceased.
Hence petitioner is considered as the dependent of the deceased.
Hence issue no1 is answered in the affirmative.

11. Issue No.2 :- Petitioner has categorically contended that on the date of accident, that on 17.01.2021 at about 00.50 a.m., the deceased Vijaya Kumar and others were returning to Bengaluru in Canter lorry bearing No.KA-02-C-8008 and when they reached near Metatukri of Hariyuru Taluk, the said Center lorry got punctured, since it was midnight no mechanic was available, they decided to stop the vehicle by the side of road.

They got down from the vehicle and some of them slept in front of the vehicle and some of them were sitting, at that time the driver of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AC-2285 ( here in after called the offending vehicle ) which came from Davanagere to Bengaluru side on NH-4 road in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, lost control over the said vehicle, dashed against the stationed vehicle, result of which the vehicle which was stationed moved ahead and ran over the persons who were slept side in front of the vehicle and deceased was succumbed to fatal injuries.
12. In order to substantiate the petition averments, the petitioner got examined herself as PW1.
In the examination in chief, she has reiterated the petition averments.
In support of the contention, she has produced 9 documents which are at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
Among them Ex.P1 is the FIR, EXP2 is the FIS, Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot sketch, Ex.P.5 is the PM report, Ex.P.6 is the MVA report and Ex.P.9 is the Inquest mahazar.

13. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Mounesha, case has been registered against the drivers of the Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 and offending vehicle in Crime No.0019/2021 of Hiriyur Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 283, 337, 304(a) IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the drivers of Canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-C-8008 and offending vehicle bearing for the offence punishable under Section Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67624714/
3 279,337, 283, 304-A of IPC.
14.

entities.text: Section Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
Though the petitioner has contended that rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident and though the respondent no.1 in his written statement has contended that the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of canter lorry and deceased is the sole cause for the accident but if the FIR and charge sheet is perused, it clearly reveals that the complaint was lodged by the co driver of the offending vehicle and in the complaint he has stated that on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle by name Yesu by driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner from Davenagare towards Bangalore hit against the canter lorry which was parked by the side of road without taking any precaution in dangerous position,
result of which both the vehicles sustained damages and the deceased and another who were slept in front of canter succumbed to the injuries.

Though the respondent no.1 in its written statement and though the complainant as RW.1 in his evidence in chief has stated that the driver of their vehicle is not responsible for the accident and that the driver of the canter lorry alone is liable for the accident but the complaint which is given first in point of time coupled with the charge sheet which clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle has also contributed negligence.
15. If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road is nearly 36 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the extreme left side of Chithradurga - Bangalore road.
The canter lorry was parked on the extreme left side of the road.
Nowhere either in the petition or in the police documents there is any whisper about any indication put on the canter while parking the vehicle in the night hours on the road.

When any vehicle is stationed by the side of road in the day hour or night hour they have to give/ put necessary indication so as to give caution to the other vehicles passing through the said road about the vehicle stationed in the said road.
At the same time when the accident in question has occurred at 12-50 a.m. i.e., in the mid night no much vehicle would ply in the said road.
When the road is sufficiently wide, the driver of the offending vehicle could have driven his vehicle by leaving sufficient space in the left side of the road.

Further had he driven his vehicle in slow and steady manner, this accident could have been avoided because from the head light of the offending vehicle the parked vehicle could be visible at a little distance and at that time if the offending vehicle is driven in a slow or in normal speed, on seeing the parked vehicle from the head light, the driver of offending vehicle could have applied break and could have avoided the accident.
Hence, it can be said that the driver of both the vehicles have contributed negligence.

Hence considering the materials available on record it can be said that the negligence contributed by the driver of the canter lorry is at a ratio of 40% and of the offending vehicle at the ratio of 60 %.
Hence, issue no.2 is answered in the partly affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:-

It is the contention taken by the petitioner that she being the mother of the deceased is the dependent of the deceased and that deceased was working as stunt master in Cinema Industry and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
17.
It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 23 years.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card of the deceased which show his date of birth as 23-05- 1992 and as the accident took place in the year 2021 it can be said that deceased was aged about 29 years as on the date of accident.

Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67624714/
4 18.
As it is observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioner that deceased was working as stunt master in Cinema Industry and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m..
Admittedly there is no document placed to prove the income of the deceased.
When there are no materials to prove the income of the deceased, court has to take the notional income of the deceased to assess the quantum of compensation under the different heads.
19. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned,
in order to prove the same petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence taking in to consideration the age of the deceased and the year in which accident in question has occurred, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs 15,000/- p.m.
20.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as he was bachelor 50% of annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

21. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

Hence in the instant case as the victim was 29 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%
22.
Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- on which 40% is added towards future prospect which comes to Rs.21,000/-.
Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10, 500/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is 17 for the age of the deceased.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.21,42,000/- (10,500x 12 x 17).
23. Because of untimely death of deceased the petitioner has lost her son, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

24. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67624714/
5

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: parental consortium and filial consortium.
This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
25.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioner due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
 SL Heads Amount  1 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/-
 Funeral Expenses

2 Loss of love and Rs. 48,400/-
 affection  3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-

4. Loss of Dependency Rs.21,42,000/-
 Total Rs.22,26,700/-
Thus, in all petitioner is entitled to Rs.22,26,700/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
26. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on Issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the respondent no.1 and 2 to pay the compensation at the ratio of 60: 40.

Hence, the respondent no.1 being the owner of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AC-2285 is liable to pay compensation to an extent of 60% and remaining 40% compensation shall be paid by the respondent no.2 being the owner of the canter lorry bearing No.KA-02-C-8008.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.4: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.22,26,700/- + cost of Rs.500/- order on IA-II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.22,27,200/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakh Twenty Seven Thousand Two Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.22,26,700/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Mahadevamma.M vs Mile Motor Service on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67624714/

6 The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay 60% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.13,36,020/- +
Rs.500/- with interest there on at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.

The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay 40% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.8,90,680/-
with interest there on at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
Out of compensation awarded to petitioner and interest
, 50% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
